### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c962e0d923565cb525e1947dd7780feb8f64f2eb` — the merge of head `1fc44a469f46d82643a528c0cd61cfca75af8737` into base `0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c962e0d923565cb525e1947dd7780feb8f64f2eb && git checkout c962e0d923565cb525e1947dd7780feb8f64f2eb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2 1fc44a469f46d82643a528c0cd61cfca75af8737 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2 && git merge --no-ff 1fc44a469f46d82643a528c0cd61cfca75af8737

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0e4b0fa411de344a0c2f38500255c68fc1cdfdf2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Not awaited; this record judges the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Save door refuses what the registry refuses — asked of one code path.** `SchemaRegistry.registerObject`'s four pre-materialization doors moved whole into private `judgeRegistrationDoors`; `registerObject` calls it as its first statement, `objectRegistrationRefusal` returns its answer without registering. The protocol asks it with `{ ...body, _provenance: 'org' }`, `layer.packageId`, `layer.kind` — byte-identical to the write-through (`applyObjectRegistryMutation`, protocol.ts ~10576) and the boot hydration (~22345). Nothing rewrites `request.item` between the ask (~14063) and the put that the doors read: the later rewrites are protection block, operator/section grafts, parsed actions, label restoration, credential carry-forward (no-op for `object`, which has no redactor). **Right**, with two caveats judged in ④ (ordering before the Zod gate; the state-dependent door).
2. **The `extend` door is not reached by this PR.** Both call sites are under `singularType === 'object'` with `layer.kind` of `own | overlay`; `object_extension` saves and publishes are not asked. The changeset and PR body list "an `extend` contribution it refuses" among what is now refused at save. **Wrong as written** — overclaims the narrowing (should-fix in ④).
3. **The field-`type` door adds no narrowing at the save door.** `resolveOverlaySchema('object')` is the kernel `ObjectSchema`, whose field `type` is the closed `FieldType` enum and required; `findUndeclarableFieldType` admits exactly `FieldType.options`. The Zod gate at ~14600 already refused every such body with `422 INVALID_METADATA` and structured `issues[]`. The registry door now answers the same body first, same code and status, no `issues`. Accept-set unchanged; envelope changed. **Wrong as an accept-set claim**, and a should-fix on the envelope (④).
4. **Promote door.** `promoteDraftForPublish` asks the same question on `draftForGate.body` inside the D9.9 block, before `repo.promoteDraft`; `publishPackageDrafts` promotes through it and its per-item catch tags and rethrows into the batch catch that builds `failed[]` / `batch_aborted` (ADR-0067 D2). A pre-rule draft carrying an author `queue` is refused by name (pinned). **Right.**
5. **Existing stored rows still load.** `loadMetaFromDb` is untouched: no refusal added at hydration; an `owner_id`-echo row registers as before (author field) until re-saved or migrated; a `queue`-echo row never registered on `main` and still does not until repaired. Boot registers the `convertStoredItem`-converted body while save/promote judge the raw body; no ADR-0087 conversion today rewrites an object field `type` or a `summary` roll-up (checked the conversion surfaces under `packages/spec/src/conversions` and `migrations/entries`), so no save/boot disagreement exists at this head. **Right**, noted as a latent coupling.
6. **Translated-echo restoration (pure half).** Runs for every `object` save before `stripServedObjectColumns`, comparing only against `injectedSystemColumnDefs(item)` (gated by the same `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` plan the read uses). A translated `queue`/`owner_id` becomes the platform definition and the existing byte-identical strip removes it; `isInjectedColumnDefinition` unchanged. **Right.**
7. **Translated-echo restoration (stored-row half).** Source = `storedBodyForCarryForward` (draft row → active row → code layer), after every refusal, before the put. The comparison is per slot, name-keyed, and requires `value !== source` and `value === read(source)` for some locale; a slot the source does not declare is never compared; the same-reference contract holds when nothing changes. Locale set = bundle keys ∪ `BUILTIN_SYSTEM_FIELD_LABEL_LOCALES`: the read resolves any `Accept-Language` to one of those rows (exact → case → base → variant, `localeChain` only reorders within the same keys) or translates nothing, so every string the read could have served is tried. Cost: at most 2 sources × (|bundle| + 4) `translateObject` calls over a document pruned to the incoming field names — bounded by field count. **Right as to coverage and cost; wrong in one reachable case** (must-fix, ④ item 1): the module translates the stored source without `packagedBase`, the read translates with it.
8. **New export `BUILTIN_SYSTEM_FIELD_LABEL_LOCALES`** (`@objectstack/spec/system`, via `export * from './i18n-resolver'`): `readonly string[]`, frozen, derived from `SYSTEM_FIELD_LABELS` by construction, placed beside the table whose read rule it describes; `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` carry the matching one-line additions; Spec property liveness green; one consumer in-tree (the echo module). **Right.**
9. **`SchemaRegistry.objectRegistrationRefusal`** (`@objectstack/objectql`): additive public method, parity-pinned against the throw in `ownership-queue.test.ts`. **Right.**
10. **Migration (`os migrate meta --stored`)**: `translated-label-echo` notices per slot, comparing the row with itself and the platform's injected definitions; `--apply` re-saves through the door. Author-field translations stored before this rule are not repaired by it (the row is its own source) — the PR says so. `surface: 'object.field.label'` is stamped on object-level and option slots too — cosmetic. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29673-translated-echo-save-door.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec` all `patch`; title `fix(metadata-protocol)!: …`; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; Skills-docs line present. PR body carries the same two declaration lines. Check Changeset: `success`.

**`!` at `patch` is right under this repo's rule.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone; `none` takes `patch`; "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". A new export is not a metadata-protocol kind. `none` holds: no key, value or default an author can write changed meaning; the one refusal this PR makes real at the door (an author's own `queue` on a user-owned object, ADR-0142 D3; a record-currency `summary` pair) is the registry's on `main` already, so nothing an author could successfully publish is refused now. The alternative reading (`narrowed` ⇒ `minor`) would describe a value the protocol accepted, which it never did — the save stored it and the registry refused it.

**Clause-②: no (narrowing)** — right in kind; the sentence overstates what the tree narrows (①.2 and ①.3): the `extend` door is never asked, and the field-`type` door was already closed by the spec gate. Should-fix to make the declaration match the tree (④ item 3).

SCHEMA face (spec addition): judged in ①.8 — right, additive, generated surfaces regenerated and matching.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, freeze: `protocol.ts` frozen for #25467 section 3; every hunk pushed before the freeze; PR stays draft, rebases after the lift. The brief names the delta review. **Answered** — this record is of the head as it stands.
- Dev flag, residual post-commit catch: `applyObjectRegistryMutation`'s `console.warn` stays for failures the pre-flight cannot see (state-dependent record-currency door). **Answered, and escalated in ④ item 5**: the same door disagrees in the other direction too, which the PR does not name.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: ui card owed (Studio edits the translated read and PUTs it back whole) — the seat files it; agreed it is not this PR's lane.
- Card "Wanted" item 3: a repair for stored rows — delivered (migration) and pinned; a zh-CN leg on `studio-authoring.first-run-loop` — stated for the seat to route; the dogfood case drives the real REST doors on the booted showcase.
- The `Skills-docs: none` line names `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` (Ownership queues) as already teaching the `queue` refusal; not re-read here (prose face), accepted on its face since the rule it teaches is unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: ADR-0142 D3 refuses an author's own `queue` on a user-owned object at registration, and ADR-0029 D9.9's producer-side refusal is the stated pattern for "the receipt and the registry agree because the write never happens". Moving that refusal to the door that stores the body makes the spec's own refusal real; it removes no declared capability — nothing on `main` declares that an author may store a translated read as the document (the i18n-resolver header says display-name resolution is a read-exit concern). The restoration half is the write-side inverse the read exits owe (same door as `stripReadDecorations` / `stripServedObjectColumns`). The shape is right. Findings against the tree:

1. **must-fix — the stored-row restoration translates its source without `packagedBase`; the read it inverts translates with it.** `protocol-translated-echo.ts` `translatedSource` calls `translateObject(doc, bundle, { locale })`; the REST read calls it with `packagedBase: packagedObjectBaseOf(...)` (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3040`), under which a slot that diverged from the packaged text is served untranslated in every locale (`valueOverridesPackagedBase`, ADR-0029 D9.2a). The catalog is name-keyed, not value-keyed, so for a packaged object whose stored overlay slot already diverged (say `title.label` renamed from `Title` to `Subject`, bundle zh-CN `objects.X.fields.title.label = 标题`), an author who now types `标题` has the save store `Subject` again, with `200` and no notice: `标题` is not a translation of `Subject` and the read could never have served it for that slot, so this is outside the declared rule ("equal to the translation of its source") and outside the declared edge — it is an author's edit discarded silently on a non-echo path, which is the class the card's rule names (loud over silent). Reachable from Studio by any tenant customizing a packaged object with a catalog. Fix: hand the module the packaged base (the code layer `storedBodyForCarryForward` already falls back to) and pass it as `packagedBase` to every `translateObject` call in `translatedSource`, so the module's reads are the read's; or skip a stored slot whose value already differs from the packaged base. The pure half (platform definitions) is unaffected. Pin: a diverged overlay slot set to the catalog string is kept.
2. **should-fix — the restoration is silent on the save answer.** `restoreTranslatedEchoes` returns `restored[]`; the door discards it. The sibling on the same door (`droppedWithheldKeyNotices`, #28640) puts every dropped position on `advisories`. Put each restored slot (`path`, `from`, `to`) on `advisories` so the author who hit the declared edge is told; the migration already says it per slot.
3. **should-fix — the changeset's Clause-② sentence names refusals the tree does not add.** "an `extend` contribution it refuses" — no call site asks with kind `extend` (①.2); "a field `type` the registry refuses" — already refused by the Zod gate on `main` (①.3). Either tighten the sentence to the two doors this PR makes real (an author's own `queue`; a record-currency `summary` pair) or wire the `object_extension` save/publish doors to ask with `'extend'`, which widens the PR.
4. **should-fix — the registry ask precedes the spec gate, changing the envelope for an already-refused body.** At ~14063 the field-`type` door answers before the Zod gate at ~14600; a body with an absent or unknown field `type` now gets `ObjectFieldTypeRefusedError` (no `issues[]`) instead of the spec gate's `INVALID_METADATA` with `issues[].path` that Studio highlights (#5364, #10524). Same status and code, so no accept-set change; but the structured path is lost. Ask the registry after the spec gate (it costs no read), or keep the ask where it is and let the field-type door's answer fall through to the gate.
5. **should-fix — the state-dependent door disagrees with registration in both directions; the PR names one.** `recordCurrencySummaryRefusal` reads the registry as it stands. Named: pre-flight accepts, registration refuses (a sibling in the same batch completes the pair) — stays in the `console.warn`. Not named: a draft save is refused `422` against the live registry although the batch it belongs to would register it (the child's amount leaves record-currency mode in a sibling draft promoted first). Rare, but it is a refusal at save of a draft a publish can serve, which #23712's premise does not cover. Either state it beside the named residual, or ask that one door in publish mode / at promote only (where `pending` / `batchObjects` could be consulted) and leave the two pure doors on the draft save.
6. **should-fix — a new, undeclared fail-closed read on every object save.** `restoreTranslatedObjectEchoes` reads the stored row on every `object` save (before this PR the door read it only for types with a redactor — `object` has none). With no stored row it falls to `readCodeLayerForCarryForward`, which asks the metadata service first and throws `throwMetadataServiceUnavailable` when the service is degraded and the registry has no entry — the case of a brand-new object, which has no source to compare beyond the platform definitions the pure half already handled. That is a new `503` on a first object save under a degraded control-plane service, declared nowhere. Either treat "degraded and not in the registry" as "no source" for this restoration (the credential carry-forward's fail-closed reason does not transfer: there is no credential to lose), or name it in the changeset.

Observations, no fix owed: boot judges the converted body and save the raw one (①.5) — no conversion touches the doors today, but a future field-`type` conversion would open a save/boot disagreement; the migration stamps `object.field.label` as the surface of object-level and option slots; `objectRegistrationRefusal` fails open on a registry without the method (partial doubles only).
